name: Flock Safety
summary: Flock Safety sells camera, license-plate recognition and investigative software to public-safety customers. Its March 2025 financing valued the company at $7.5 billion.
overview: Flock Safety combines networked cameras, automated license-plate recognition and software for public-safety investigations.

facts.label: Latest disclosed valuation
facts.note: Flock announced the financing was led by Andreessen Horowitz.

bull_case: A growing camera and software network can create data and workflow advantages for customers as public-safety agencies consolidate tools.
bear_case: Privacy concerns, public scrutiny, policy changes and procurement risk can constrain expansion or raise the cost of maintaining trust.
directory_notes: Watch privacy governance and recurring-software adoption.

intelligence.description: Public-safety technology platform combining cameras, automated license-plate recognition and investigative software.
company: Flock Safety sells hardware and software used by law enforcement, neighborhoods and businesses to investigate incidents. Its platform combines cameras, automated license-plate recognition and software workflows.

The company announced a $275 million financing at a $7.5 billion valuation in March 2025. The central strategic question is whether it can scale a sensitive public-safety network while maintaining privacy safeguards and customer trust.
intelligence.why_it_matters: Flock is a significant private-market example of a hardware-plus-software network business. Its trajectory shows both the appetite for public-safety technology and the governance risks that can shape adoption and valuation.

changed.text: Flock announced a $275M fundraise at a $7.5B valuation.

takeaways: Network density can improve product value but increases governance responsibility.
Privacy and procurement scrutiny are core investment risks.
The $7.5B valuation came from a disclosed financing.
